files.description: Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

task_text: Going down riders.csv in file order and comparing home_district values without regard to capital letters or surrounding spaces, mark every rider whose home_district is Harbourside while the rider just above has Riverbend. `result` should hold one True/False value per rider, in file order (False for the first rider).
intended_computation: Read riders.csv; d = home_district stripped and lower-cased, in file order; flag[i] = (i > 0 and d[i] == "harbourside" and d[i-1] == "riverbend"); 400 booleans in file order.

acceptable_variants.notes: flags may be booleans, 0/1 or a list

intent_summary: In a column of text states, flag each row whose state is B while the row just before it has state A (a two-row sequence A then B).

column_map.states A and B (placeholders): A = riverbend, B = harbourside (first two distinct values in file order, compared without capital letters and stray spaces)
